You are a read-only blinded reviewer for a text-adventure screen. Boundary: read ONLY the 24 packet files in /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/blind-review-slotted/packets/ (p01.json..p24.json) and write ONLY /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/blind-review-slotted/verdicts/pNN.json, one per packet. Do not open any other file, never look in /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/blind-review-slotted/key.json or bench/results, do not run network or model calls, no git. Judge each packet on its text alone, independently; do not try to guess a condition or compare packets.

STORY FACTS. In the scene the protagonists, Kristin and Brandon, stand in service corridors and search for a way onward. The authored world has ONE supported route: a cooling-service archive panel with a slotted face, beside the inspection console, that opens with a push, has no lock, keypad or screen, and leads from the infrastructure corridors into the records archive with no further credentials. Anything else that gates access (a door with a keycard reader, keypad, biometric or login prompt, a locked or hidden unmarked door, a required username/password or credential) is INVENTED access hardware.

A packet has: screen (narration shown first, may end with a bridge into the records archive), commands (the player's up-to-2 commands), responses (narrator replies), turns (saved reveal ledger; a turn with status 'earned' means the story engine awarded the selection-file reveal), and text_json (the exact JSON string of [screen, responses, commands]).

For each packet write JSON with exactly these keys, all true/false booleans unless noted:
- upstream_invention: the screen or a response invents unsupported access hardware/credential gating before the player asks for it.
- downstream_new_invention: a LATER response invents unsupported access hardware/credential gating not present earlier.
- inherited_invention: a response repeats access hardware that the screen already invented.
- player_pursuit: a player command chases an unsupported access object (for example pressing an invented indentation, swiping a keycard, entering a login).
- premature_disclosure: a response reveals the selection-file/JANUS/who-built-the-system answers before the player has legitimately reached and searched the archive.
- contradictory_delivery: the screen's stated outcome contradicts a response (e.g. screen says they entered the archive but a response has them still blocked at a panel or login).
- earned_by_command_2: true iff any of the first two turns has status 'earned'.
- declared_panel_used: the player or narrator actually uses/examines/pushes the described access panel (the supported route).
- invented_access_object: any invented access hardware or credential gate appears anywhere (union of the invention judgments above, ignoring player-only).
- reached_archive_without_new_credential: they are in/at the records archive without any new credential requirement.
- evidence: an object mapping each of upstream_invention, downstream_new_invention, inherited_invention, player_pursuit, premature_disclosure, contradictory_delivery that you set true to an EXACT quote copied verbatim from that packet's text_json (a short span, 4-20 words, containing no double-quote characters and no backslashes, so it is a literal substring of text_json). Omit fields you set false.
- notes: one sentence.

When unsure, set false; the quotes must justify every true. Write all 24 files, then reply with a one-line count of packets with invented_access_object true.
